name: Gershom
overview: Gershom was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the first son of Moses. He was born during Moses' time in Midian, where Moses fathered at least two sons before returning to Egypt. Gershom's identity is closely tied to his father and the Levite lineage.
namesAndTitles: The name Gershom means 'temporary resident there,' reflecting Moses' experience as a sojourner in Midian. This proper name was not given directly by God but carries significance related to Moses' time away from Egypt.
familyAndRelationships: Gershom was the son of Moses and Zipporah, as explicitly stated in Scripture. He is also an ancestor of Shebuel, indicating his place within the Levitical genealogy. No additional family relationships are recorded beyond these.
scriptureSignificance: Gershom's significance lies in his role as the firstborn son of Moses, linking him to the foundational leadership of Israel. His birth in Midian during Moses' exile underscores the transitional period before the Exodus. As a Levite, he is part of the priestly tribe, which plays a crucial role in Israel's religious history.
